light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld home video shot by her grandson with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered kitchen background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the window a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, age spots and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes and apron with real creases and flour dust. People are caught mid-action, unposed. Daylight from the window on the left plus the ceiling lamp.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by her grandson with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the kitchen in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural old hands; she moves naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

anchors.prompt: Same kitchen, same moment of the day. Loretta, an 81-year-old woman with short curly white hair, light-framed glasses, a pearl necklace, a lilac cardigan over a lilac blouse and a floral apron with a green trim, old hands with age spots and veins sits at the floury wooden table of her 1950s white farmhouse kitchen: a white enamel stove, yellow checked curtains on the window at the left, a ceramic rooster on the wooden dresser, a small wooden cross on the wall, a paper church calendar, a floury wooden table with a worn spiral recipe book. In front of her on the table sits a whole golden chess pie in a clear glass pie plate, its top shiny and a little crackly, and she holds a table knife just above it, about to cut, looking at the camera and talking. Medium shot from about one and a half meters, the pie and her upper body in frame, the stove and the rooster behind her.

A few seconds later, same place: she has cut a slice and lifts it on a metal pie server toward the camera, the pale yellow custard inside trembling, one wedge missing from the pie, her face delighted and a little proud, eyes on the slice.

Same place a few seconds later: the slice now sits on a small flowered plate beside the pie, she looks up above the camera at her grandson with a warm, amused half smile, both hands resting on the table, the pie server laid down.
Same place: she leans back a little in her chair and opens one hand toward the pie on the table, nodding firmly, a stubborn little smile, as if saying she still does it herself.

Same kitchen, same light, the pie now pushed aside with one slice missing. She sits with both hands flat on the closed worn spiral recipe book, eyebrows raised, a knowing, slightly skeptical look at the camera, mid-sentence.
Same place a few seconds later: she taps the cover of the closed recipe book twice with one finger, lips pressed together, shaking her head slightly, unimpressed.

Same place: she leans toward the camera and lowers her head a little as if telling a secret, holding up between two fingers a small faded, stained, yellowed old recipe card written in pencil, the recipe book open behind her hand.
Same place a few seconds later: she slides the small faded recipe card back into the back pages of the open recipe book, looking at the camera with a small secretive smile, one eyebrow up.

Close view of the golden chess pie in its glass plate on the floury table, filling the frame: her old hand holds a table knife whose blade is pressed into the shiny crackly top, starting the first cut. Her wrist and lilac cardigan sleeve enter from the right edge.
Same close view a few seconds later: a metal pie server lifts a wedge out of the chess pie, the pale yellow custard of the cut side soft and glossy, a crumb of crust falling.

Close view on the floury wooden table of her kitchen: a pale cream colored sugar cream pie in a glass plate, unbaked and liquid, and her old hands grate a whole nutmeg on a small metal grater over it, the first brown specks landing. Her lilac sleeves enter from the top edge.
Same close view a few seconds later: the top of the pale pie is covered with fine brown nutmeg freckles, her hands still grating.

Close view on the floury wooden table: an unbaked pie crust in a glass plate filled with dark shiny molasses filling, and her old hand scattering brown sugar crumbs over it from a yellow mixing bowl, the crumbs falling. Her lilac sleeve enters from the right edge.
Same close view a few seconds later: the dark molasses is now covered with an even layer of brown crumbs, a few crumbs still falling from her fingers.

Close view on the floury wooden table: a lemon pie with bright yellow filling in a glass plate, a thick layer of fresh white meringue spread on top, and her old hand holds a rubber spatula touching the meringue. Her lilac sleeve enters from the right edge.
Same close view a few seconds later: the spatula has pulled the meringue up into many tall curled peaks all over the pie.

Close view of the white enamel stove of her kitchen: a black cast iron skillet on the burner, melted butter foaming in it, and her old hand stirring dark brown sugar into it with a wooden spoon. Her lilac sleeve enters from the right edge, the yellow checked curtain at the edge of the frame.
Same close view a few seconds later: the butter and brown sugar in the skillet have melted into a bubbling dark amber syrup, the wooden spoon still stirring, a thin wisp of steam.
Close view of the white enamel stove: a small dented saucepan of simmering water with a cup of dark raisins in it, small bubbles, steam rising, a wooden spoon resting on the rim.
Same close view a few seconds later: the raisins have plumped up, round, shiny and soft, bobbing in the simmering water, more steam.

Close view on the floury wooden table: an unbaked pie crust in a glass plate, a box of round butter crackers without any label beside it, and her old hands breaking a round cracker in half over the crust, a few big cracker pieces already inside. Her lilac sleeves enter from the top edge.
Same close view a few seconds later: the bottom of the crust is covered with big broken cracker pieces, her hands dropping one more piece.

Close view on the floury wooden table of her kitchen: the worn spiral recipe book lies closed, its red cloth cover faded and stained, her old hand resting on it, flour dust around, a rolling pin at the edge.
Same close view a few seconds later: the recipe book lies open to a yellowed page covered in old handwriting in blue ink with grease spots, her hand flattening the page.

clips.text: Now you put that camera right down here, honey, because nobody makes this one anymore. Look at that. See how it shivers?
clips.action: She talks to her grandson behind the camera while she slides the knife into the chess pie and lifts the slice on the server toward the camera, delighted. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: There were seven pies on every church table I ever knew. And after nineteen seventy, they just... disappeared. Well, I still bake every one of them.
clips.action: She puts the slice down, looks up at her grandson and talks, a little wistful, then leans back and nods firmly at the pie. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: And I'll tell you what I think happened to them. It wasn't that they stopped tasting good. It was a little box of mix... and a tub from the freezer case.
clips.action: She talks with her hands on the closed recipe book, skeptical, then taps the cover with one finger. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.

clips.text: And the last one, the one my mother made back in the war years? There's a trick in it I have never shown anybody. We'll get there.
clips.action: She leans toward the camera holding the small faded recipe card, speaking lower as if telling a secret, then slides the card back into the book with a small smile. She wears the same lilac cardigan, pearl necklace, light-framed glasses and floral apron with the green trim the whole time.
